newsitem.title: UK: UKs Rifkind says Labour muddled on Europe.
newsitem.headline: UKs Rifkind says Labour muddled on Europe.

text.p: Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind, setting aside dramatic differences within Britain's ruling Conservative Party over the European Union, on Thursday described Labour's European policy as "incoherent and muddled".

Rifkind, speaking at a Conservative election news conference, said "one day (Labour leader) Tony Blair swears he will never be isolated in Britain. The next day he says he would be proud to be isolated."
"One day Mr Blair pledges to be a friend of the EU by abandoning the national veto in numerous areas. The next day he is threatening to use it."
Rifkind said Blair had already exposed his "naive incompetence" by announcing what position he would take at the Amsterdam EU summit in June six weeks before it took place.

"Not even the French and the Germans have given any indication of the concessions they might make at Amsterdam. Chancellor (Helmut) Kohl and President (Jacques) Chirac are far too experienced and astute. They would eat Mr Blair for breakfast and digest him for lunch."
